title: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects
summary: Automated search and fine-tuning produced a large set of synthetic training datasets with surprising model-behavior side effects. Held-out scoring and a human study support a specific finding about training-data generalization; the source limits it to synthetic, mostly single-turn behaviors, with some effects unstable across retraining.
ai_technology: Automated search and language-model fine-tuning for synthetic training data
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Results §§4–5 report 6,575 datasets across eight behaviors and show that effects can be induced by ordinary-looking synthetic data; the study investigates a specific LLM generalization phenomenon.
evidence.unknown: Section 5 uses held-out metrics and Section 6 has 25 ML researchers annotate 64 datasets; human prediction is 63% versus 50% chance and the automated scores track judgments, with limitations stated in §7.
evidence.ai_role: Methods §§3–4 use model fine-tuning, evolutionary/RL/subliminal search, and held-out LLM scoring to generate datasets with target behavior effects.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
